prediction:
1. Bacillary angiomatosis (Bartonella henselae/quintana) — immunocompromised host on chemotherapy; multiple tender vascular papules/nodules on trunk/neck are classic; PCR/biopsy with Warthin–Starry stain or empiric macrolide response would support diagnosis.
2. Ecthyma gangrenosum from Pseudomonas (or other gram-negative bacteremia) — immunosuppressed patients can develop tender necrotic/ulcerating lesions on trunk; fits systemic risk from chemotherapy and cytopenias.
3. Disseminated cutaneous staphylococcal infection (including MRSA abscesses/folliculitis) — multiple tender pustular/nodular lesions possible in immunocompromised patients.
4. Sweet syndrome (acute febrile neutrophilic dermatosis) — associated with hematologic/oncologic disease and some chemotherapies; painful erythematous plaques/nodules on upper body can mimic infection.
5. Cutaneous involvement by underlying malignancy (cutaneous plasmacytomas/leukemia cutis or metastatic lesions) — less common but possible with relapsed hematologic malignancy and can present as tender nodules.

Key missing data that would change ranking: morphology of lesions (vesicular/pustular/ulcer/violaceous vascular papule), presence of fever/systemic signs, distribution dermatomal vs diffuse, presence of central venous port, blood cultures, lesion bacterial/fungal culture, lesion biopsy with histology and special stains/PCR, and platelet trend/bleeding signs.
